solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Confine temper when the game is safe

parts.note: to confine something is to close it in
to temper food or speech is to season it, moderate or flavour it

explanation.surface: An instruction to restrain one's mood at a moment when a match is risk-free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' here means hunted animals and birds, not a sporting contest; they are protected by law for part of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: The close season is the legal period in which shooting or fishing a species is banned, so the quarry is protected.

indicators.note: the deficit word sits inside the fuel word, splitting it

parts.note: coal is a common fuel
a deficit is a loss

explanation.surface: A complaint about an enormous shortfall in energy supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something colossal is enormous in size.

indicators.note: disrupted means the letters of the word Antihero are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A flawed protagonist upset a radio or TV transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme going out live or being transmitted is said to be on air, an idiom for broadcasting.

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Ethiopian

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: An Ethiopian head of state formally starts a sporting competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' reads as a verb about starting the tournament, but it is the noun for a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting tournament is a competition or contest, which is also called an event.

clue.text: Ref once failed to put into effect

indicators.note: failed suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of Ref once are disordered

explanation.surface: A football referee who used to officiate once failed to apply the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a law into effect is to make sure it is obeyed, which is what enforcing it means.

indicators.note: the wrongdoer word goes around the quiet letter, enclosing it

parts.note: an evildoer is a sinner
P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer surrounds a silent cricket player.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a spinner is a bowler who makes the ball turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinner is a type of cricket bowler who puts spin on the ball, so a kind of cricketer.

clue.text: Men dare to change in cathedral

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of Men dare to

explanation.surface: Men are bold enough to swap clothes inside a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like changing clothes; it is the anagram signal on MEN DARE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is the famous Gothic cathedral in Paris, an example of the category.

definitions.meaning: to press lightly with a cloth

explanation.definitionFit: Dab is both a light pressing touch with a cloth and a small flatfish related to the plaice.

indicators.note: the cynical word goes about the operations word, around it

parts.note: dry humour is cynical, sardonic
ops is short for operations

explanation.surface: Someone sceptical about surgery as a cure for disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropsy is an old name for oedema, an ailment where fluid swells the body.

clue.text: Ridin' on island in the Pacific

parts.note: ridin' is a shortened riding, so biking with the final G dropped likewise

explanation.surface: Someone riding along on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Ridin'' signals that the synonym also loses its final G: BIKIN'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini Atoll is located in the Pacific, in the Marshall Islands, site of US nuclear tests.

parts.note: lit means illuminated
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A highlighted note appears in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' suggests a book; it is a measure of capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric unit measuring capacity, a quantity of volume.

clue.text: Troop keeps absorbent material for gun

indicators.note: keeps means the troop word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a troop or crowd can be a flock
lint is a soft absorbent fabric for dressing wounds

explanation.surface: A body of soldiers carries wadding for its firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A flintlock is an old type of firearm fired by a flint striking steel.

indicators.note: splits means the novice word breaks the polish word apart, sitting inside

parts.note: polish is a shine, a sheen
a tiro is a beginner

explanation.surface: A beginner divides a Polish metal tray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to look like the nationality, but it is polish, a gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheet iron is iron rolled into thin flat plates, a metal sheeting.

clue.text: Weaken after losing pounds in Germany

indicators.note: after losing means the weaken word has the pounds letter removed

parts.note: to lessen is to weaken or reduce
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (libra)

explanation.surface: An economy weakening after its currency has fallen in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city located in the Ruhr region of Germany.

parts.note: tissue is a fine web or network, as in a tissue of lies

explanation.surface: A computer network is being debated.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a matter at issue is the point currently being debated.

clue.text: Go away with list that can be bagged

parts.note: shoo is said to tell someone to go away
a table is a list of figures

explanation.surface: A hunter departs with an inventory of game.
explanation.walkthrough: To bag game is to shoot it.
explanation.definitionFit: Game that can legally be bagged by a hunter can be shot, so is fit to shoot.

definitions.meaning: the stern of a ship is its back end
to parent a child is to bring it up, raise it

explanation.definitionFit: Rear means the back part, like a ship's stern, and as a verb to bring up children.

clue.text: Nut rowed out into awkward current

indicators.note: out means the letters of Nut rowed are disordered

explanation.surface: A crazy oarsman rowed out into a tricky stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' reads as a madman doing the rowing; it is just letters for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertow is a dangerous current beneath the surface pulling away from shore.

clue.text: Nosy parker adopts child of convict

indicators.note: adopts means the nosy word takes the child word in

parts.note: a prier is a nosy person who pries
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A busybody takes in the offspring of a jailbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict serving a sentence is held in jail, hence a captive inmate.

indicators.note: after places the runs letter behind the snake

parts.note: a boa is a large snake
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A creature dashes after a serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a wild pig or uncastrated male pig, a kind of beast.

indicators.note: about means the embarrassed word goes around the exhaust word

parts.note: red-faced, so red, means embarrassed
to tire is to exhaust

explanation.surface: Someone who departed red-faced about a car's exhaust pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhaust' looks like the car part; it is the verb to wear out.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to withdraw or go away, so retired can mean departed.

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
leaner times are poorer ones

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie becomes more impoverished every day.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'daily' is a domestic cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: British usage: a daily is a cleaning woman who works in someone's house by day.

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected

indicators.note: some means only part of the word horses is used, its opening letters

explanation.surface: A bug spray had an effect on several horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' reads as acted upon, but it means camp, mannered; 'some' keeps HOR, dropping the final SES of horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Camphor is a strong-smelling compound used in mothballs to keep insects away.

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A mother asks for some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a rich patterned woven cloth, originally from Damascus.

clue.text: Wait for veteran to strike out

indicators.note: out means the strike word sits outside the veteran word

parts.note: to hit is to strike
old means veteran

explanation.surface: Waiting for an old soldier to be dismissed by a bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a command telling someone to stop and pause where they are.

parts.note: A is a grade for first-class
a bout is a boxing or wrestling match

explanation.surface: A top-level cricket game takes place in the vicinity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First-class match' suggests cricket; it splits into a grade and a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: About as an adverb means in the vicinity, around here.

parts.note: a supply teacher is a temp, a stand-in
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Providing a door fastening for a warning alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' and 'lock' read as verb and fastener; they are a stand-in worker and some hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren in myth lured sailors, so any seductive woman is a siren.

parts.note: a shot of spirits is a tot
a sovereign is a pound coin, abbreviated L

explanation.surface: Firing at a gold coin, then claiming the result beyond dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is a British gold coin worth one pound, and L is the pound sign's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Total as in total certainty means complete and absolute, not open to question.

clue.text: Hurled bag out of festival site

indicators.note: out of means the letters of Hurled bag are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone threw a bag out of a festival ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldeburgh is a Suffolk coastal town, home of the music festival founded by Benjamin Britten.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldeburgh hosts a well-known annual music festival in England.

clue.text: It is consumed by bronze colossus

indicators.note: consumed by means the word It is swallowed inside the bronze word

parts.note: tan is a bronze colour, as of skin

explanation.surface: A statue made of bronze swallows something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bronze colossus' calls up a giant statue such as Rhodes'; bronze is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a giant person or thing, like the mythical Titans.

indicators.note: some means only a part of skittles is taken

explanation.surface: Provides a few bowling pins.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit means equipment or gear, the supplies needed for an activity.

clue.text: Blossom makes church official initially feel let down

parts.note: an elder is an official in some churches

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter of feel

parts.note: to lower is to let down

explanation.surface: A clergyman feels disappointed by a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let down' looks like disappointed but means lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderflower is the creamy blossom of the elder tree, used in cordials.
